listings.description:
Madison is fortunate to have a number of venues that provide a free community meal so everyone can enjoy this holiday geared toward giving thanks for a plentiful harvest and giving back to the community. This year we’re down one, though; Delta Beer Lab, which long hosted a turkey day table, closed permanently in October. Still at it: First Congregational United Church of Christ-Madison offers a traditional T’Day meal via delivery or pick up at the church on Thanksgiving between noon and 3 p.m. RSVP required; call 608-233-9751 or visit <a href="https://www.firstcongmadison.org/">firstcongmadison.org</a> by 3 p.m. Nov. 19 to place your order. Registration is required for the meal at Lakeview Lutheran Church, 4001 Mandrake Road (noon, doors open at 11:50 a.m.; RSVP at 608-244-6181; reservations are capped at 100 for sit-down and 50 for takeout). Slice's Bar &amp; Grill serves a pay-what-you-can donation carryout dinner as a Christmas fundraiser for kids' toys; you must call the bar at 608-243-6925 by Nov. 23 to reserve a meal, and meals can be picked up from 11 a.m.-2 p.m. on Thanksgiving Day. Check Facebook for updates. Drop-in options on the holiday include Good Shepherd Lutheran Church, 5701 Raymond Road (11 a.m.-1 p.m.); and Luke House, 310 S. Ingersoll St. (4-5 p.m.). &#13;

UW Russian Folk Orchestra Weekly Practice/Rehearsal
listings.description:
The UW Russian Folk Orchestra, now in its 30th season, is an ensemble performing Slavic and East-European folk music on authentic instruments, balalaikas, domras, and bayans. Come join us! We'll teach you how to play our instruments, and you'll become a member of our very unique and fun group!
Ability to read music is highly desirable.

listings.title: WUD Film Committee Weekly Meeting
listings.description: UW-Madison students of all majors and levels of interest in film are welcome to join the WUD Film Committee—the only membership requirement is a love for movies.  WUD Film—a student-led team—hosts hundreds of diverse, innovative, and exciting movies for the University community.  Committee members help curate our film programming, manage our weekly screenings, and learn valuable leadership skills in the process.

listings.title: Stories Across Generations
listings.description: Settle in for a special storytime that brings generations together. Eleanor Dougherty shares beloved picture books with young listeners in a warm, welcoming setting. This gentle program invites children ages 0–8 and their caregivers to connect through stories, imagination, and the simple joy of reading together.

listings.title: Let’s Move! with Abby
listings.description: Join us for movement games and activities! From obstacle courses to dances, group games and balance activities, we’ll enjoy different opportunities to move our bodies every day. Program location is subject to change, depending on the weather. Please check our Welcome Wall for the most up-to-date location information. This event is free with general museum admission.

listings.title: Music Time with Tim
listings.description: Explore the world of music and rhythm! Each week, Tim leads children in singing and other musical activities that inspire creativity and connection. It’s an engaging experience for kids and families—free with admission.

listings.title: Clay Day
listings.description: Squish it, shape it, roll it, and build with it! Each week, Laurie and museum staff lead a new hands-on project featuring air-dry, polymer, or ceramic clay. Learn techniques for shaping and decorating while giving yourself plenty of room to experiment. Whether you’re making something practical, playful, or completely unexpected, Clay Day is a chance to discover what your hands and imagination can create.
